maya: Quick sanity check — new 7B reranker (rk7b-ptq) on anchor_v2 shows ~-0.03 NDCG on the holdout. Anyone else seeing this?
sam: Yep ran offline earlier. MRR roughly same, NDCG dip seems concentrated on long-tail queries (rare tokens / long docs).
andre: Which anchor set + metric window? NDCG@10 or @100? Also which tokenizer/version used during PTQ?
maya: anchor set = anchor_v2_core+longtail, metric = NDCG@10. PTQ run used tokenizer from the PTQ build pipeline (HF tokenizers v0.13). Our prod harness uses v0.15.
ci-bot: CI: rerank-eval/anchor_v2_core+longtail queued — baseline (fp16) vs rk7b-ptq. Result snapshot: NDCG delta = -0.031 (p=0.009) — see logs: https://ci.internal/rerank/4320
ashley: Quick ideas: (a) tokenizer mismatch sounds plausible, (b) candidate ordering differences (topk truncation), (c) KV packing changes during quant build. Also check if prefix-caching+batching changed effective context.
li: Also remember PTQ can shift embedding scale slightly — try per-dim rescale or embed-postnorm. We saw small tail regressions from that before.
sam: I'm going to run a tokenizer-parity check: reproduce the PTQ eval but force HF v0.15 tokenization pipeline so we know if tokenization is the main factor. Command I plan to run:
```
python -m eval.rerank --model rk7b-ptq --anchors anchor_v2_core+longtail --tokenizer-version 0.15 --metric ndcg@10 --seed 42
```
Should be quick on small split.
andre: Also check that the offline harness uses the same topk for candidate generation. Last time a mismatch between offline topk=100 and prod topk=10 caused weird NDCG moves in tail slices.
maya: Good point — our eval script used topk=100 by default. The production gated metric is @10. I'll re-run with topk=10 to match.
nashley: For ablation plan:
- A: FP16 baseline (existing)
- B: PTQ as-is (v0.13 tokenizer, topk=100)
- C: PTQ with tokenizer parity (v0.15), topk=10
- D: PTQ + embed-rescale post-processing
Also include seeds [42,73,128] and compute slice-wise NDCG for longtail vs core.
li: Don't forget to pin batch sizes / KVpack toggles. PTQ runtime sometimes uses different packing heuristics under batch>1 which changes KV cache boundaries. Run with `--batch-size 1` and `--kvpack false` too.
sam: I'll take tokenizer parity + batch/kvpack parity tests. maya will run the full ablation including embed-rescale.
ci-bot: Acknowledged. Jobs queued: 4321 (ptq-tokenizer-parity), 4322 (ptq-kvpack-batch-parity), 4323 (ptq-embed-rescale-ablation). ETA ~2h depending on GPU queue.
maya: Thanks. One more ask — when computing significance, use bootstrap on query-cohort rather than docs to avoid underestimating variance on tail queries. Also include effect sizes (Cohen's d).
andre: Noted. Also capture candidate ordering logs for a handful of failing queries so we can inspect whether truncation changed the winning candidate. Put them under `s3://redwood-debug/rerank/1795550001/` if possible.
nashley: If ablation points to tokenizer, we should add a tokenizer-parity check to the PTQ pipeline (fail-fast) and a golden prompt set for tail queries.
maya: Agreed. I'll post results back here once the runs finish. @ci-bot please ping when jobs complete :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Jobs 4321-4323 started. Will post artifacts + summarized slice metrics when done.
li: If we see small but consistent loss only on longtail, consider a quick patch releasing quant with slight embedding-scale adjustment — low risk and we can roll back.
maya: Cool. Closing loop for now. Running first batch with seeds now.
ci-bot: Update: job 4321 finished — tokenizer parity removed ~60% of the NDCG gap. Full artifacts: https://ci.internal/rerank/4321/artifacts.json
maya: Nice — that's a strong signal towards tokenizer drift. I'll analyze artifacts and then run embed-rescale test.
sam: Will also push a tiny script to check tokenization diffs for failing queries. Quick diff example attached in artifacts.
ci-bot: Update: job 4322 & 4323 queued; ETA ~30m.
